title: The Sages Who Went to Indra
word: the three doshas as a way of noticing
hook: sick sages send one of their own up to Indra, and he brings back the science of life
carry: health is the root of dharma
tomorrow: a boy fasts fifteen days and forgets his Vedas. why?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Sushruta's word for well, svastha: health that ends in a clear mind.

The Charaka Samhita, one of Ayurveda's oldest texts, opens with a problem, not a cure. Great sages, the story says, had given their lives to prayer, study and self-discipline, and illness kept getting in the way. Bodies gave out before the work was done. So they gathered on a slope of the Himalaya to ask one question: who can help us? And one of them, the sage Bharadvaja, stood up and said: send me.
screen: `A PROBLEM, NOT A CURE.` → `ILLNESS IN THE SAGES' WAY.` → `BHARADVAJA: SEND ME.`

segments.voice: Bharadvaja climbed to Indra, king of the gods, who had received this knowledge, the text says, in a line reaching back to Brahma. Indra taught him the science of life, Ayurveda: ayus, life, and veda, knowledge. He taught it in three parts: the causes of illness, its signs, and what heals. Bharadvaja came back down and taught the sages, and one of them, the teacher Atreya, passed it to six students, one of whom first wrote it down. And here is the line the story is built to deliver. The sages say health is the best root of the four aims of life: dharma, doing what's right; artha, a livelihood; kama, love and joy; and moksha, freedom itself. Illness robs all four. That's a Hindu teaching, said plainly: the body isn't the enemy of the spiritual life, and caring for it isn't vanity. It's the ground the rest grows from. Even the sages needed it. So what does this science see? One verse of the Ashtanga Hridaya, a later classic, gives the doshas a clock: kapha at the beginning, pitta in the middle, vata at the end, of a day, a night, a meal, a whole life. A slow morning may not be a character flaw; some of it may be the hour. On this path that's a way of noticing, never a diagnosis, and anything that keeps on goes to a doctor. And today? The night you skip dinner to study, the week you run on four hours of sleep, the sages would say you're digging up the root.
screen: `INDRA TEACHES BHARADVAJA.` · `HEALTH: THE ROOT OF THE FOUR AIMS.` · `THE BODY IS THE GROUND.` · `KAPHA, THEN PITTA, THEN VATA.`

segments.voice: Sit and feel the body as it is right now: heavy, warm, light or scattered, and notice what part of the day it is. Then, if you pray, thank God for this body, the ground of the four aims, in your own words or a prayer you know. If you don't pray, thank it anyway. It has carried every good thing you've done.
The three doshas, as a way of noticing. Today, the story of how this science came down from Indra, and the line it carries: health is the root of dharma, artha, kama and moksha.
Your line: health is the root of dharma. Even the sages needed well bodies to pray. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Many Hindus see care for the body as part of dharma. Ayurveda, which tradition often links to the Atharva Veda, tells its own beginning as Bharadvaja learning the science of life from Indra for the sake of the sages, and teaches that health is the root of the four aims of life; its dosha clock is used on this path only for noticing.
